papers.titleEn: High-Efficiency Perovskite-Organic Tandem Solar Cells Enabled by Perovskite Crystallization Optimization and Metal-Free Interconnecting Layer
papers.abstract: Perovskite-organic tandem solar cells (PO-TSCs) offer a promising route toward high-efficiency and cost-effective photovoltaics by combining wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskite solar cells (PSCs) with narrow-bandgap organic solar cells. Nevertheless, achieving high-performance PO-TSCs still faces key challenges: open-circuit voltage ( V OC ) loss in the WBG perovskite sub-cell and optoelectrical loss at the interconnecting layer (ICL). Here, we incorporate 4-nitrophenethylamine hydrochloride (4N-PEACl), a functional additive bearing a strong electron-withdrawing group (-NO 2 ), into the WBG perovskite precursor solution to modulate crystallization kinetics and passivate bulk defects. This additive significantly improves crystallinity and phase stability, suppresses non-radiative recombination and enhances charge extraction and transport. Consequently, the optimized 1.85 eV WBG single-junction PSC achieves a champion efficiency of 19.79%, with V OC increasing from 1.349 to 1.388 V. Furthermore, the optimal PO-TSC achieves an efficiency of 27.10% with an ICL of PCBM/AZO/SnO 2 /PEDOT:PSS/Ph-4PACz. This work highlights the efficacy of -NO 2 -functionalized molecules in improving WBG perovskite film quality and provides new design strategy for low-cost but effective ICLs in PO-TSCs.
papers.filename: Fei Huang, Adv. Mater., 2026, High-Efficiency Perovskite-Organic Tandem Solar Cells Enabled by Perovskite Crystallization Optimization and Metal-Free Interconnecting Layer

papers.titleEn: Buried Interfacial Transport Governs Oxide-Protected Electrocatalysis
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Protective overlayers are widely used to stabilize metal catalysts under harsh electrochemical conditions. Unlike graphene coatings, oxide overlayers introduce a buried metal-oxide interface that fundamentally reshapes reaction pathways by separating proton delivery from product release. Although proton transport through oxides has been extensively investigated, the fate of reaction products at buried interfaces remains unresolved; for example, H2-molecule vs H-atom pathways remain under debate in oxide-protected hydrogen evolution. Here, we revisit this buried interface using a microelectrochemical cell with well-defined model structures. Systematic measurements across nine metal-oxide heterostructures, combined with density functional theory calculations, reveal that product transport is governed by two sequential kinetic barriers: hydrogen spillover across the metal-oxide junction and hydrogen permeation through the oxide lattice. These coupled barriers determine whether reaction products are released, accumulate at buried interfaces, or induce interfacial failure. This work not only identifies superior Pt-TiO2 and Pd-TiO2 but also clarifies which step is impeded in Au-TiO2, Pt-SiO2, Pt-HfO2, Pd-SiO2, Pd-HfO2, Au-SiO2, and Au-HfO2 heterostructures. Guided by these model studies, we implement a TiO2 protection strategy in a proton-exchange-membrane water electrolyzer with remarkable durability. These findings provide a framework for constructing a complete proton-to-product route for buried interfaces, potentially resolving long-standing ambiguities in oxide-protected electrocatalysis.
papers.filename: Shuangyin Wang, J. Am. Chem. Soc., 2026, Buried Interfacial Transport Governs Oxide-Protected Electrocatalysis

papers.titleEn: An Interfacial Electron Pump Enhanced Photo-Assisted CO 2 -to-Bioplastic Microbial Electrosynthesis
papers.abstract: Most solar- and electrochemical CO 2 -utilization strategies still terminate in small-molecule products, whereas direct access to recoverable carbon products such as bioplastics remains uncommon. Here, we develop a photo-assisted bioelectrochemical platform by coupling a Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 bioanode functionalized with Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene quantum dots (MQDs) to a Cupriavidus necator biocathode modified with Ni-doped carbon dots/poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (Ni-CDs/PDDA). Cell-associated MQDs form a conductive and photoactive biointerface, operationally described as an interfacial electron pump, that facilitates lactate-dependent extracellular electron transfer (EET) under applied anodic bias and adds an illumination-dependent current contribution. The MQDs-enabled microbial fuel cell (MFC) delivers a peak power density of 0.82 ± 0.03 mW cm -2 under illumination. In the coupled CO 2 -fed system, anodic illumination raises polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) productivity to 131 mg L -1 d -1 at -0.6 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (vs. RHE), approximately 47% above the matched dark value over a 12 h interval. The coupled platform reaches an apparent total-energy-to-PHB efficiency of 3.42% when electrical, incident optical, and lactate-derived chemical inputs are included. Multiscale analyses support an EET-coupled interfacial relay involving cytochrome/heme-associated components within the native EET network. This interface-to-synthesis strategy links photo-assisted microbial electron harvesting to H 2 -mediated CO 2 -to-PHB biosynthesis.
papers.filename: Wenlei Zhu, Adv. Mater., 2026, An Interfacial Electron Pump Enhanced Photo-Assisted CO 2 -to-Bioplastic Microbial Electrosynthesis

papers.titleEn: Ultrarobust and Thermo-Mechano-Photo-Responsive Elastomers by Supramolecular and Dynamic 3D Topological Architectures
papers.abstract: Mechanically robust elastomers are being widely used in multi-stimuli-responsive systems including closed-loop recycling, information encryption, and advanced photolithography. However, their advancement is hindered by an inherent trade-off: structural integrity for mechanical robustness versus molecular-level reversibility for stimuli responsiveness. In this study, we constructed ultrarobust recyclable and photo-responsive supramolecular-dynamic covalent networks (SDCN) based on molecular engineering of anthracene-functionalized poly(urethane-urea-amide) (PUUA) networks with hindered urea motifs. Well-designed SDCN achieves multiscale assembly through coordinated π-π stacking, hydrogen bonding, and dynamic covalent interactions, creating dynamic coupling between soft-chain crosslinks and self-assembly hard domains, and driving microphase separation. Under stretching, strain-activated disassembly of dynamically assembled nanostructures synergizes with stress-induced crystallization, in situ evolving three-dimensional topological architectures and promoting strength-toughness enhancement. Consequently, PUUA elastomers exhibit remarkable mechanical performance (100.17 MPa tensile strength, 1286.79% elongation and 498.15 MJ m -3 toughness at room temperature; 113.67 MPa strength and 667.8% elongation at -40°C) and recycling performance (92.4% recyclability via solvent reprocessing). Significantly, UV-responsive anthracene photonic moieties combined with temperature-mediated interfacial SDCN transition enable fluorescent encryption and sub-micron photolithographic patterning. Therefore, this work coordinates dynamic thermal-mechanical-optical responses and multi-scale molecular transition mechanisms, which can be expected to boost high-precision photolithographic patterning and flexible microcircuit printing fields.
papers.filename: Hezhou Liu, Adv. Mater., 2026, Ultrarobust and Thermo-Mechano-Photo-Responsive Elastomers by Supramolecular and Dynamic 3D Topological Architectures

papers.titleEn: Ligand-Framework Reactivity Contrast Enables Programmable Threshold Fluorescence Switching in MXene Quantum Dots
papers.abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) is both a biologically relevant redox species and a common transduction product in oxidase-catalyzed assays, making its concentration indicative of biological redox status or clinically important substrates such as glucose. However, most H2O2 detection methods produce continuously varying signals and therefore lack a distinct visual readout at physiologically relevant decision thresholds, limiting rapid point-of-care assessment. Here, Asc-Ti2C QDs with a ligand-framework architecture were designed to generate a visible readout at a defined H2O2 threshold. The contrasting reactivities of the ascorbate ligands and Ti2C framework produced an abrupt fluorescence transition, and this threshold could be systematically tuned by adjusting the ligand-to-framework ratio. As a proof-of-concept application, the Asc-Ti2C QDs were coupled with glucose oxidase, immobilized in a PVA/PVP matrix, and integrated into a cassette for hypoglycemia screening. The resulting device exhibited a readily visible fluorescence transition at 4.0 mM glucose, close to the 3.9 mM hypoglycemia alert threshold, enabling direct naked-eye identification without instrumental quantification. Overall, this work advances fluorescence sensing beyond continuous quantification toward direct readout of biologically relevant thresholds, enabling more rapid and actionable diagnostic decisions.
papers.filename: Yan Li, Anal. Chem., 2026, Ligand-Framework Reactivity Contrast Enables Programmable Threshold Fluorescence Switching in MXene Quantum Dots

papers.titleEn: Spatially Internalized InP@ZnS Quantum Dots Facilitate Bifunctional Catalysis for High-Efficiency Photo-Driven PHB Biosynthesis
papers.abstract: Semiconductor-biological hybrid systems show potential for sustainable biomanufacturing but are limited by high transmembrane resistance, rapid photogenerated carrier recombination, and a single catalytic mode. We constructed a spatially compartmentalized dual-pathway biohybrid by integrating core-shell InP@ZnS quantum dots (QDs) in vivo into Cupriavidus necator H16. Intracellular QDs directly inject photogenerated electrons via near-field coupling into redox centers, promoting NADP+ and NAD+ reduction, while extracellular QDs photocatalytically generate H2, which acts as a diffusible auxiliary electron carrier, further elevating the pools of NADPH, NADH, and ATP. Under this dual-pathway configuration, peak bulk NADPH/NADP+ and NADH/NAD+ ratios increased by 37.8% and 48.6% (single-cell increases of 26.8% and 37.8%), and total ATP rose by 50.6% during the logarithmic growth phase and by 33.9% at the single-cell level. Without external mediators and under low ambient light (4200 lx), the hybrid achieved a polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) titer of 6.55 g L-1, which was 2.18-fold higher than that of the light control, representing the highest enhancement reported for C. necator H16-based systems. The ZnS shell suppresses carrier recombination and reduces metal ion leakage, thereby improving stability. This work demonstrates a dual-pathway electron-delivery strategy for microbial production of sustainable materials and presents a generalizable approach that integrates internalization of QDs, dual-pathway electron transfer, and passivation with the ZnS shell.
papers.filename: Shaoqin Liu, ACS Nano, 2026, Spatially Internalized InP@ZnS Quantum Dots Facilitate Bifunctional Catalysis for High-Efficiency Photo-Driven PHB Biosynthesis

papers.titleEn: A Room-Temperature Self-Healing Polymeric Additive for Efficient, Mechanically Robust, and Environmentally Durable Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) face critical challenges in long-term stability, lead toxicity, and mechanical fragility, aggravated under UV light and mechanical deformation. Here, we introduce an in situ crosslinked dynamic polymer network (PSS) as a multifunctional additive that simultaneously imparts room-temperature self-healing, crystallization regulation, defect passivation, and ion immobilization. The network enables the perovskite composite to achieve room-temperature self-healing in 10 min. Flexible PSCs incorporating PSS attain a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 24.97%, retain over 84% of initial performance after 8000 bending cycles, and recover to over 96% within 10 min. In rigid devices, the network regulates crystallization and passivates defects, yielding a champion PCE of 26.30%. Moreover, the crosslinked framework acts as a physical barrier at grain boundaries, while its abundant functional groups bind mobile ions through chelation, collectively suppressing moisture/oxygen ingress and ion migration. This synergistic effect enables over 96% efficiency retention after 1500 h of maximum power point tracking, reduces lead leakage by over 90% in water, and significantly enhances UV tolerance. This in situ crosslinked network with low T g and diphenyl disulfide bonds provides a promising platform for rapid self-healing additives toward high-efficiency, mechanically robust, and environmentally sustainable perovskite photovoltaics.
papers.filename: Tengling Ye, Adv. Funct. Mater., 2026, A Room-Temperature Self-Healing Polymeric Additive for Efficient, Mechanically Robust, and Environmentally Durable Perovskite Solar Cells

papers.titleEn: Extraction-Limited Charge Loss in Tin-Based Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.abstract: Tin-based perovskite solar cells (PSCs) present a promising lead-free alternative for photovoltaics, yet their performance remains markedly inferior to that of lead-based counterparts. A limited understanding of the underlying differences in charge transport dynamics between tin- and lead-based PSCs continues to impede efforts to overcome the reduced open-circuit voltage (Voc) and fill factor (FF) characteristic of tin-based devices. Here, using bias-modulated electrical transient measurements, we reveal a previously neglected extraction-limited charge loss mechanism in tin-based PSCs (efficiency > 14%) that is not evident in lead-based counterparts (> 25%) and fundamentally constrains both Voc and FF. Under high forward bias, the defects and their associated self-doping at the perovskite/electron transport layer interface severely reduce charge extraction efficiency by limiting the extraction of low-mobility carriers due to bulk field screening, which in turn leads to reduced collection efficiency as the unextracted carriers are forced into nonradiative recombination. This mechanism explains the low Voc and FF in tin-based PSCs and underscores interfacial doping control as critical for further performance enhancement.
papers.filename: Qing Shen, ACS Energy Lett., 2026, Extraction-Limited Charge Loss in Tin-Based Perovskite Solar Cells

papers.titleEn: Multifunctional Dendrimer Interlayers for Tin-Based Perovskite Solar Cells: Inducing Interfacial Dipoles and Suppressing Electrode Corrosion
papers.abstract: Tin-based perovskite solar cells (Sn-PSCs) offer eco-friendly optoelectronics but suffer from low efficiency and ambient instability. Here, we introduce a second-generation poly(amidoamine) (PAMAM) dendrimer interlayer between the C60/BCP electron transport layer and the Ag top electrode. Electrostatic field orientation induced by the metallic electrode activates a PAMAM dipole that shifts the effective interface work function by ∼0.55 eV. This modification of the interfacial energetics is accompanied by an increase in the open-circuit voltage (VOC) by ∼50 mV and is consistent with reduced contact-induced energetic losses. Additionally, the dendrimer forms a physical/chemical barrier against iodine-mediated electrode corrosion. Consequently, unencapsulated Sn-PSCs retain 80% of their initial power conversion efficiency (PCE) after 1000 h in ambient air (∼30 °C, 20-35% RH), a benchmark stability also demonstrated here for Sn-Pb PSCs. This electrode-induced dipole orientation presents a generalizable strategy for boosting efficiency and operational durability in lead-free perovskite photovoltaics.
papers.filename: Iván Mora-Seró, ACS Energy Lett., 2026, Multifunctional Dendrimer Interlayers for Tin-Based Perovskite Solar Cells Inducing Interfacial Dipoles and Suppressing Electrode Corrosion

papers.titleEn: Deciphering Charge Delocalization across Mercaptobenzonitrile Ligand Terminals and Inner Hydrides in Atomically Precise Cu14H10 Nanoclusters for Electrocatalytic CO2 Reduction
papers.abstract: Cu hydride nanoclusters with atomic precision in composition and structure offer exciting catalytic activities and opportunities for rigorous structure-function correlations. Determination of their atomic structures, especially the hydride locations, hinges on the availability of high-quality single crystals and neutron beams, while their relatively weak UV-visible absorption and electrochemical instability challenge the analysis of their electronic properties. Herein, we synthesize a Cu14H10 nanocluster coordinated by three 4-mercaptobenzonitrile (MBN) and eight triphenylphosphine ligands. Two-dimensional NMR analyses combined with single crystal X-ray diffraction reveal unequivocally the locations of the ten hydrides in four groups (stoichiometry ratio of 1:3:3:3) with drastically different environments (chemical shifts 11-3 ppm): one H at the inversion center and three triangular layers along the C3 axial bridging together the Cu core. MBN serves two additional purposes besides stabilizing ligands: its electron-withdrawing nature and a highly sensitive vibrational reporter of its local charge density. The first property gives rise to a low-lying Cu-core-to-MBN metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) excited state, and the second property enables direct spectroscopic probing of both the charge transfer nature and dynamics of the MLCT excited state through the dynamic spectral shift of the MBN CN stretching mode. Through combined transient IR absorption spectroscopy and time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations, we obtained the complete atomic and electronic structure, revealing core-to-ligand charge transfers in these nanoclusters. Computed under identical conditions using an iso-structure with a mildly electron-donating ligand, the Cu14H10 featuring charge delocalization toward the electron-withdrawing MBN has a smaller HOMO-LUMO gap, which is deemed favorable for electrocatalytic CO2 reduction. The preferential formation of complex multielectron-hydrogenation products (8-12 e-, C1 hydrocarbons, and C2+ products) over two-electron pathways such as CO formation or the competing hydrogen evolution reaction highlights their promise as atomically precise catalysts for deep CO2 reduction.

papers.titleEn: Proton-Pump Engineering in Photo-Responsive TiCo-MOFs for Efficient Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production
papers.abstract: The current industrial anthraquinone route to hydrogen peroxide is energy-intensive, hazardous, environmentally unfriendly and has spurred a quest for greener synthetic methods. Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production using water and oxygen is an attractive alternative, but its efficiency is often limited by the slow kinetics of water oxidation, which in turn restricts the proton supply needed for the oxygen reduction reaction. Herein, we report a proton-pump engineering strategy that precisely tailors the proton-donating capability of a stable photo-responsive TiCo 2 -based metal-organic framework (MOF) without altering its underlying framework topology. By incorporating functional groups with distinct pK a values, -NH 2 and -OH, onto the terephthalate linkers, we achieve controlled modulation of the local proton transfer kinetics. The TiCo 2 -OH MOF exhibits significantly enhanced proton conductivity, superior charge separation efficiency, and a markedly stabilized *OOH intermediate. As a result, this material delivers a high H 2 O 2 production rate of 20 525 µmol g -1 h -1 in pure water under visible light irradiation without any sacrificial agents, exceeding the best previously reported MOF-based photocatalysts under comparable conditions. This work establishes pore engineering as a generalizable, non-destructive strategy for overcoming the proton supply bottleneck in photocatalytic proton-coupled reactions, offering a sustainable platform for green H 2 O 2 synthesis.
papers.filename: Zhangjing Zhang, Adv. Funct. Mater., 2026, Proton-Pump Engineering in Photo-Responsive TiCo-MOFs for Efficient Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production

papers.titleEn: Chromophore Orientation as a Design Strategy for Self-Assembled Monolayers in p-i-n Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.abstract: Self-assembled monolayers of the carbazole-based phosphonic acids recently became a popular choice for hole-selective layers in p-i-n perovskite solar cells. However, the role of molecular geometry in controlling interfacial coverage and device performance remains poorly understood. In this work, we have investigated anchor-to-chromophore connectivity as a molecular design parameter by synthesizing four carbazole phosphonic acid derivatives with T-shape and Rod-shape structures. The molecular pairs were designed to keep similar energetic properties while varying the spatial orientation of the chromophore relative to the phosphonic acid anchoring group. Optical spectroscopy and photoemission yield measurements confirm that the energy levels are governed primarily by the substitution position on the carbazole core, rather than by molecular orientation. In contrast, electrochemical impedance and cyclic voltammetry measurements reveal pronounced differences in charge-transfer blocking ability, indicating improved ITO surface coverage for Rod-shape molecules. When implemented in p-i-n perovskite solar cells, Rod-shape interlayers provide a reproducible improvement in device performance, although in part hindered by less favorable wetting behavior. After mitigating film formation and top interface losses, devices with 3-Rod reached a power conversion efficiency of 25.04%. These results demonstrate the importance of chromophore orientation for designing densely packed, high-performance phosphonic acid materials for perovskite solar cells.
papers.filename: Artiom Magomedov, ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 2026, Chromophore Orientation as a Design Strategy for Self-Assembled Monolayers in p-i-n Perovskite Solar Cells

papers.titleEn: A Multifunctional Core-Sheath Fiber Patch Based on Cellulose Nanocrystal-Reinforced and Curcumin-Loaded Polylactic Acid for Enhanced Pelvic Tissue Repair
papers.abstract: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) affects millions of women due to tissue defect, marked by disrupted collagen homeostasis and abnormal immune reaction. Therefore, there is a demand for developing a multifunctional patch resolving these current straits. Herein, we fabricated a multifunctional core-sheath fibrous patch via coaxial electrospinning, comprising cellulose nanocrystal (CNC)-reinforced polylactic acid (PLA) sheath and curcumin-loaded PLA core. Post-electrospinning heat treatment enhanced PLA crystallinity improved mechanical properties and enabled sustained curcumin release. The patch exhibited stable degradation, good biocompatibility, and potent anti-inflammatory activity. In vivo, the CNC-PLA/Cur-h patch achieved native-tissue-comparable biomechanical strength within 4 weeks, with enhanced neovascularization, elevated collagen I/III ratio, and well-organized extracellular matrix. RNA sequencing confirmed upregulated angiogenesis and ECM-related genes, as well as downregulated inflammatory markers. This multifunctional platform integrates mechanical robustness, controlled biodegradability, and proregenerative capacity, presenting a promising strategy for POP repair.

papers.titleEn: Chloroacetate Buffer-Modified SnO2 Electron Transport Layer for Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.abstract: Tin oxide (SnO2) is a popular material for the electron transport layer (ETL) in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, the defects at the SnO2/perovskite interface tend to induce non-radiative recombination and deprotonation of formamidinium (FA+), limiting the device performance. Herein, a chloroacetate (CA) buffer system consisting of chloroacetic acid and its potassium salt was employed as a unique multifunctional interface modifier to synergistically engineer the SnO2 ETL/perovskite interface. The chloroacetate anion anchors to Sn and Pb sites, while the chloroacetic acid stabilizes FA+ through the hydrogen bond. As a result, the acidic buffer system suppresses FA+ deprotonation, enhances perovskite film quality, and improves carrier transport. Consequently, the CA buffer-modified PSC devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 24.8%, considerably higher than 22.6% for the control devices. They also demonstrate prolonged dark-storage stability; particularly, the unencapsulated devices retain 99% of initial efficiency after 1500 h of ambient storage. This work shows that combining an organic acid and its conjugated base offers a facile yet effective strategy to simultaneously passivate the buried interface and stabilize perovskite components for efficient and stable PSCs.
papers.filename: Limin Qi, ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 2026, Chloroacetate Buffer-Modified SnO2 Electron Transport Layer for Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells

papers.titleEn: Solar-Matched Colloidal Quantum Dots/Metal-Organic Framework Hybrid Materials for Photo-Induced Charge Transfer
papers.abstract: Lead sulfide colloidal quantum dots (PbS CQDs) are promising third-generation photovoltaic materials, and metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are complementary materials that are used as multifunctional charge storage and redox platforms. Hybrid materials combining CQDs and MOFs are highly promising for applications utilizing solar-driven charge transfer, but their synthesis can be challenging due to the thermal instability of solar-matched infrared CQDs. Here, we demonstrate a room-temperature, "bottle-around-ship" synthesis of a nanocomposite that integrates near-infrared (NIR) absorbing PbS CQDs with an iron-based MOF, MIL-88B(Fe). We employ a syringe-pump-assisted addition of precursors to achieve controlled nucleation and crystallization of the MOF around the CQDs under ambient conditions. Structural characterization confirms the formation of crystalline composites composed of co-localized CQDs with the MOFs. Steady-state, time-resolved optical spectroscopy reveals photoluminescence quenching and shortening of the exciton lifetime in the composite compared to the CQDs alone. Transient absorption data suggest a photo-induced charge transfer from the PbS CQDs to the MIL-88B(Fe) framework on a picosecond timescale. This work establishes a room-temperature synthesis approach for integrating thermally sensitive solar-matched CQDs with functional MOFs and performs an initial spectroscopic study to evaluate the potential of these nanocomposites as advanced hybrid materials for photocatalysis and optoelectrochemical devices in the future.
papers.filename: V. Sara Thoi, ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 2026, Solar-Matched Colloidal Quantum Dots Metal-Organic Framework Hybrid Materials for Photo-Induced Charge Transfer

papers.titleEn: Homochiral Interfacial Coupling Enables Chiroptical Amplification and Spin Regulation in 0D/2D Perovskite Heterojunctions
papers.abstract: Chiral perovskites are promising materials for circularly polarized light detection and spin-optoelectronic applications, but simultaneously enhancing chiroptical responses and regulating spin dynamics within a single system remains challenging. Here, we construct dual-homochiral 0D/2D perovskite heterostructures by integrating chiral CsPbBr 3 quantum dots with a chiral 2D perovskite framework. The homochiral interfacial coupling gives rise to markedly enhanced chiroptical responses, consistent with an interfacial modulation of the chiral lattice distortion, and enables circularly polarized light photodetection with a photocurrent dissymmetry factor (g ph ) of 0.461, 6.6 times that of the achiral quantum-dot control (0.07). Femtosecond transient absorption reveals sub-picosecond interfacial carrier transfer from the quantum dots to the 2D framework (τ CT ≈ 0.33 ps, an upper bound), while helicity-resolved transient absorption shows that the heterostructure sustains spin-polarized excited states for ≈260 ps. These findings establish homochiral interfacial coupling as an effective design element for regulating chiroptical responses and spin dynamics in chiral perovskite heterostructures.
papers.filename: Jun Wang, Small, 2026, Homochiral Interfacial Coupling Enables Chiroptical Amplification and Spin Regulation in 0D 2D Perovskite Heterojunctions

papers.titleEn: Gluconic Acid Ligand Enables Rapid Chemical Bath Deposition of SnO 2 for High-Efficiency Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.abstract: Chemical bath deposition (CBD) is widely used to prepare SnO 2 electron transport layers for high-efficiency n-i-p perovskite solar cells. However, the conventional CBD recipe using thioglycolic acid (TGA) suffers from long deposition time, nanoparticle aggregation, energy level mismatch, abundant oxygen vacancy defects, and residual thiol. Herein, we report a green and rapid CBD strategy by completely replacing TGA with gluconic acid (GA). The abundant carboxyl and hydroxyl groups of GA regulate the deposition process: they suppress nanoparticle aggregation through hydrogen bonding and steric hindrance, enabling a dense and conformal SnO 2 film within 50 min; they also promote the full oxidation of Sn 2+ , reducing oxygen vacancy defects. The resulting GA-SnO 2 promotes better energy level alignment with the perovskite film and improved interfacial charge transport. Moreover, GA inherently avoids thiol residues at the buried interface. The champion device (0.0729 cm 2 ) based on GA-SnO 2 achieves a lab-measured efficiency of 26.24%, retains 91.34% of its initial efficiency after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking, and a 5 cm × 5 cm mini-module reaches 22.23% efficiency. This work provides a rapid, green, and scalable route to high-quality SnO 2 electron transport layers.
papers.filename: Penggang Yin, Small, 2026, Gluconic Acid Ligand Enables Rapid Chemical Bath Deposition of SnO 2 for High-Efficiency Perovskite Solar Cells
